title: Hotend heater sensor disconnected
shortDescription: Prusa firmware detected the hotend temperature is below the minimum — sensor likely disconnected.
fullDescription:
Error 10 on MK3/MK4 indicates the hotend thermistor reads below the minimum threshold. The firmware assumes the wire is broken or the connector on the Einsy/xBuddy board has come loose. The heater is immediately disabled.

On the MK3 this often correlates with a worn Einsy connector or damaged hotend wiring near the flexible cable bundle at the hotend.

On the MK4 it usually points to the nextruder PCB connector.

causes.cause: Thermistor wire broken near hotend flex bundle

fixSteps.title: Reseat hotend connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open the electronics cover and reseat the thermistor connector on Einsy (MK3) or xBuddy (MK4).

fixSteps.title: Inspect flex bundle
fixSteps.instruction: Flex the hotend harness while monitoring temperature — erratic readings mean broken conductor.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new Prusa PT1000 (MK4) or 100k NTC (MK3) thermistor.

whenToCallPro: If the Einsy/xBuddy connector pad is damaged.

faq.q: Is my thermistor NTC or PT1000?
faq.a: MK3/MK3S use 100k NTC. MK4 uses PT1000.

title: Hotend maximum temperature exceeded
shortDescription: Hotend temperature exceeded the safe maximum — thermistor shorted or heater stuck on.
fullDescription:
Error 11 indicates the hotend temperature is above the firmware limit. Usually the thermistor wires have shorted together, giving a false high reading. Rarely, the MOSFET has failed closed and the heater is actually running.

Check for shorts before heating again — if the heater is actually stuck on, the hotend can reach dangerous temperatures.

causes.cause: Thermistor wire shorted near heater block

fixSteps.title: Power off immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the printer to ensure the heater is not stuck on.

fixSteps.title: Inspect thermistor wire
fixSteps.instruction: Check for melted insulation between thermistor leads near the heater block.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new thermistor with PTFE sleeving on the leads.

whenToCallPro: If MOSFET on xBuddy has failed.

faq.a: Yes, because firmware cut power. But investigate before re-enabling the heater.

title: Heating failed — thermal anomaly
shortDescription: Hotend or bed did not reach target temperature within expected time.
fullDescription:
Error 13 triggers when the printer fails to heat as expected — the measured slope is too low. Common reasons: print fan blowing on the heater block, a loose heater cartridge, or cold ambient air without a silicone sock.

Prusa's firmware is stricter than stock Marlin and catches marginal heater cartridges early.

causes.cause: Part cooling fan running during heat-up

fixSteps.title: Install silicone sock
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a genuine Prusa silicone sock over the heater block.

fixSteps.title: Tighten heater cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Let hotend cool. Tighten the M3 heater setscrew in the block.

fixSteps.title: Re-run PID tune
fixSteps.instruction: In menu: Calibration → PID Calibration → Hotend.

whenToCallPro: If heater cartridge keeps failing after replacement.

faq.q: Why does it fail in cold rooms?
faq.a: Cold ambient draws heat faster than the cartridge can supply.

title: Filament sensor not responding
shortDescription: The IR or optical filament sensor is not returning valid data.
fullDescription:
MK3S uses an IR sensor in the extruder that detects filament presence. Misalignment, dust on the sensor, or a loose ribbon cable prevents detection.

MK4 uses a loadcell-based system; errors there typically point to the nextruder cable or PCB.

Recalibrate the sensor from the menu after cleaning.

causes.cause: Loose ribbon cable to extruder PCB

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out the sensor cavity with compressed air and wipe with IPA on a cotton bud.

fixSteps.title: Recalibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Menu → Calibration → Filament Sensor Calibration. Follow prompts.

fixSteps.title: Check ribbon cable
fixSteps.instruction: Remove extruder cover and reseat the FFC ribbon cable.

whenToCallPro: If the extruder PCB is damaged.

faq.q: Can I disable the filament sensor?
faq.a: Yes, in Settings → Filament Sensor → Off.

title: Multi-material unit fault
shortDescription: MMU unit failed to load, unload, or select a filament.
fullDescription:
The Prusa MMU3 / MMU2S handles up to 5 filaments. Errors happen when filament tips are badly shaped, Bowden tubes are misaligned, or the selector cannot find the pulley position.

Most fixes involve cleaning the FINDA sensor, trimming filament tips, or adjusting the Bowden length.

fixSteps.title: Cut clean filament tip
fixSteps.instruction: Trim the filament to a sharp point, remove any blobs.

fixSteps.title: Clean FINDA
fixSteps.instruction: Remove FINDA, blow out, ensure the ball moves freely.

fixSteps.title: Check Bowden length
fixSteps.instruction: Verify all 5 Bowden tubes are equal length and fully seated.

whenToCallPro: If the MMU PCB is not detected at all.

faq.q: Why does FINDA fail more on PLA?
faq.a: PLA tends to form long strings during retract — trimming helps.

title: Mesh bed leveling did not complete
shortDescription: The PINDA/SuperPINDA probe could not level all mesh points.
fullDescription:
Prusa printers probe a 7x7 mesh using the SuperPINDA inductive sensor. If the probe cannot trigger on one of the steel sheet calibration points, mesh leveling fails.

Usually a dirty print sheet, incorrect PINDA height, or thick paint/dirt on the Y-axis dots is the cause.

fixSteps.title: Clean calibration points
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the steel sheet and clean the 9 calibration points with IPA.

fixSteps.title: Adjust PINDA height
fixSteps.instruction: PINDA bottom should be ~1mm above the nozzle tip.

faq.a: Yes — textured and smooth sheets have different Z offsets.

title: Power panic triggered or recovery failed
shortDescription: Printer detected a power loss or failed to resume after one.
fullDescription:
Prusa's Power Panic feature saves state when input voltage drops. When power returns, it tries to re-home and continue. If the saved state is corrupt or the bed has shifted, recovery may fail and require manual restart.

Frequent power panics without actual outages indicate a failing PSU or loose 24V connector.

fixSteps.title: Check 24V wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Power off. Tighten PSU terminal block and Einsy input screws.

fixSteps.title: Move to dedicated circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Plug the printer directly into a wall outlet, not a shared strip with large appliances.

fixSteps.title: Test PSU voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure 24V output under load — should stay within 23.5-24.5V.

whenToCallPro: If PSU replacement is needed and you are not comfortable with mains wiring.

faq.a: No — it's integral to Prusa firmware.

title: XYZ homing failed
shortDescription: Printer failed to home all three axes during start.
fullDescription:
MK3S and MK4 use sensorless homing (stallguard) on X and Y. If belts are too loose or too tight, stallguard never triggers or triggers too early, causing homing to fail.

On MK4 an additional XY calibration step uses the loadcell — if the nextruder loadcell is not calibrated, homing can fail.

causes.cause: X/Y belt too loose for stallguard

fixSteps.title: Check belt tension
fixSteps.instruction: Use Belt Tuning menu → target 260-290 Hz on MK3S.

fixSteps.title: Re-run XYZ calibration
fixSteps.instruction: Run full XYZ calibration from menu.

faq.a: The driver detects a motor stall instead of using a physical switch.

title: First layer calibration needed or failed
shortDescription: Live-Z offset is wrong and needs recalibration.
fullDescription:
Prusa uses Live-Z to adjust the nozzle-to-bed distance. If the first layer is too far or too close, the print lifts or smears. Recalibrate whenever the sheet, hotend, or SuperPINDA changes.

Typical Live-Z ranges from -0.600 to -1.300. Values outside this range suggest the SuperPINDA mount is wrong.

fixSteps.title: Run First Layer Cal
fixSteps.instruction: Menu → Calibration → First Layer Cal. Adjust Z in real-time until lines are uniform.

fixSteps.title: Use per-sheet profiles
fixSteps.instruction: Save a separate Live-Z for each sheet (smooth/textured/satin).

whenToCallPro: Not needed — this is routine calibration.

title: Built-in self test failed
shortDescription: Selftest found a fault in fans, heaters, motors, or sensors.
fullDescription:
Prusa MK4 selftest checks fans, heaters, endstops, and motors during first-boot and after firmware updates. It reports which component failed so you can target the fix.

Fan failures are the most common — bearings wear out after ~2000 hours.

fixSteps.title: Read detail
fixSteps.instruction: Note which step failed (hotend fan, print fan, loadcell, etc.).

fixSteps.title: Replace failing fan
fixSteps.instruction: Order genuine Prusa replacement and swap per official guide.

whenToCallPro: If loadcell selftest continues to fail after recalibration.

title: Extruder skipping steps
shortDescription: Extruder motor cannot push enough filament — causing under-extrusion.
fullDescription:
The Prusa direct-drive extruder skips steps when back-pressure is too high. Causes include a partial nozzle clog, too-high print speed, too-low temperature, or a worn Bondtech drive gear.

Update temperature and speed before replacing hardware.

causes.cause: Print temp too low for filament

fixSteps.title: Raise print temp
fixSteps.instruction: Increase hotend temp by 5-10°C; ensure flow matches filament.

fixSteps.title: Cold pull
fixSteps.instruction: Perform a nylon cold pull to remove debris from nozzle.

faq.a: Yes — the click is the gear slipping on the filament.

title: Stallguard detected an unexpected stall
shortDescription: A TMC driver detected a motor stall mid-move.
fullDescription:
Prusa firmware uses stallguard both for homing and for crash detection. Unexpected stalls mid-print pause or abort the job and display a crash message.

Causes include a blob on the print hitting the nozzle, a rod that needs lubrication, or a belt too tight.

fixSteps.title: Resume or restart
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect print for damage, resume if safe.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate rods
fixSteps.instruction: Apply a light PTFE or lithium oil to all smooth rods.

fixSteps.title: Retune belts
fixSteps.instruction: Run belt tuning in menu — target 260-290 Hz.

faq.a: Yes — it's designed to pause and offer resume.
